title: RESERVOIR CELEBRATES 2027 GRAMMY® NOMINATIONS
summary: The 2027 Grammy® nominations were announced this morning, and Reservoir congratulates our talented global roster of songwriters, artists, and partners on an incredible 43 nominations. Please see the full list below:
body_markdown:
The 2027 Grammy® nominations were announced this morning, and Reservoir congratulates our talented global roster of songwriters, artists, and partners on an incredible 43 nominations. Please see the full list below:


- **Album of the Year –** ‘Lost Weekend’ by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Album of the Year –** ‘THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.’ by RAYE, featuring “Click Clack Symphony.” feat. Hans Zimmer
- **Album of the Year –** ‘you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love’ by Olivia Rodrigo, featuring “my way,” co-written by Steph Jones
- **Best Alternative Music Album –** ‘Lost Weekend’ by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Alternative Music Performance –** “Kill Me” by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Arrangement, Instruments And Vocals –** “Click Clack Symphony.” by Raye feat. Hans Zimmer
- **Best Arrangement, Instruments And Vocals –** “The Governor’s Waltz” by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Audio Book, Narration, Storytelling Recording –** ‘Remix Meditation’ by Lil Jon
- **Best Bluegrass Album –** ‘So Much For Goodbyes’ by Billy Strings, featuring “Carry Us Home,” co-written by Joe Henry
- **Best Contemporary Country Album –** ‘Middle of Nowhere’ by Kacey Musgraves, featuring “Mexico Honey” and “Hell On Me,” co-written by Steph Jones
- **Best Contemporary Country Album –** ‘Cherry Valley’ by Carter Faith, featuring “Arrows (Die For That Man),” “Grudge,” & “Still A Lover,” co-written by Steph Jones
- **Best Contemporary Instrumental Album –** ‘Somni’ by Snarky Puppy, Metropole Orkest & Jules Buckley
- **Best Country Duo/Group Performance –** “Phone, Keys, Wallet” by Lainey Wilson and John Mayer, co-written by Jon Decious
- **Best Country Song –** “Phone, Keys, Wallet” by Lainey Wilson and John Mayer, co-written by Jon Decious
- **Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical –** ‘Middle of Nowhere’ by Kacey Musgraves, featuring “Mexico Honey” and “Hell On Me,” co-written by Steph Jones
- **Best Historical Album –** ‘Classic V-Disc Big Band Sessions’ by Various Artists featuring Reservoir catalog cuts “Dance With A Dolly” and “Moonglow”
- **Best Jazz Performance –** “I Get Along Without You Very Well, (Except Sometimes)” by Nicole Zuraitis, Christian McBride, Gilad Hekselman and Dan Pugach, co-written by Hoagy Carmichael
- **Best Jazz Vocal Album –** ‘With Every Breath I Take’ by Cécil McLorin Salvant, Metropole Orkest & Jules Buckley, featuring “Lush Life,” written by Billy Strayhorn
- **Best Jazz Vocal Album –** ‘The Devil I Knew’ by Nicole Zuraitis, featuring “I Get Along Without You Very Well, (Except Sometimes)” with Christian McBride, Gilad Hekselman and Dan Pugach, co-written by Hoagy Carmichael
- **Best Latin Pop Album –** ‘NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO’ by Karol G, featuring “BbY WOW,” which samples “Coolie Dance Riddim” by Cordel Burrell, and “Después de ti” feat. Greg Gonzalez
- **Best Music Film –** ‘Lilith Fair: Building A Mystery – The Untold Story,’ featuring “All I Wanna Do,” “Every Day Is A Winding Road,” and “If It Makes You Happy” by Sheryl Crow, “Big Yellow Taxi” by Joni Mitchell, and “Sock It 2 Me” by Missy Elliott, which samples “Ready or Not Here I Come (Can’t Hide from Love)” by The Delfonics
- **Best Music Video –** “Lost Boys” by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Music Video –** “Click Clack Symphony.” by Raye feat. Hans Zimmer
- **Best Pop Duo/Group Performance –** “Click Clack Symphony.” by Raye feat. Hans Zimmer
- **Best Pop Vocal Album –** ‘THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.’ by RAYE, featuring “Click Clack Symphony.” feat. Hans Zimmer
- **Best Pop Vocal Album –** ‘you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love’ by Olivia Rodrigo, featuring “my way,” co-written by Steph Jones
- **Best Progressive R&B Album –** ‘BERNARR.’ by Durand Bernarr, featuring “SHARP!,” co-written by Marcus “MarcLo” Lomax
- **Best R&B Album –** ‘Kehlani’ by Kehlani, executive produced and co-written by Khris Riddick-Tynes, and featuring “Call Me Back” feat. T-Pain & Lil Jon, “No Such Thing” feat. Clipse, co-written/co-produced by Oak Felder & Jayme Silverstein, and “You Got It,” co-written/co-produced by Oak Felder, Jayme Silverstein & Oscar Linnander
- **Best R&B Album –** ‘To Whom This May Concern’ by Jill Scott, featuring “To B Honest” feat. and co-written by JID
- **Best R&B Album –** ‘Brown (The Chocolate Edition)’ by Chris Brown, featuring “Colours,” co-written/co-produced by Fraka
- **Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance –** “Sweet Nuthins” by Kehlani feat. Leon Thomas, co-written/co-produced by Khris Riddick-Tynes
- **Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance –** “To B Honest” by Jill Scott feat. JID
- **Best R&B Solo Performance –** “Out The Window” by Kehlani, co-written/co-produced by Khris Riddick-Tynes
- **Best R&B Song –** “Out The Window” by Kehlani, co-written/co-produced by Khris Riddick-Tynes
- **Best Rap Album –** ‘AM I THE DRAMA?’ by Cardi B, featuring “Salute,” co-written by 2 Chainz
- **Best Rap Performance –** “LET ‘EM KNOW” by T.I.
- **Best Rap Song –** “LET ‘EM KNOW” by T.I.
- **Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical –** “WHERE IS MY HUSBAND! – Remix” by RAYE, David Guetta, and Hypaton
- **Best Rock Performance –** “Lost Boys” by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Rock Song –** “Lost Boys” by Phoebe Bridgers
- **Best Traditional Folk Album –** ‘The Fiddle And The Drum’ by Renée Fleming with Béla Fleck, featuring “The Fiddle and the Drum” feat. Jerry Douglas, written by Joni Mitchell
- **Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical –** Tony Berg
